patterns: when to use more instead of er
entries.answer: A comparative measures two things and takes -er or more, as in taller and more careful, while a superlative measures a whole group and takes -est or most. The irregular set is small but worth learning as pairs, so good, better and best, and far and further. The rule people get wrong is the length limit, where more is required beyond about three syllables because an -er form stops being readable, and mixing the two is the usual slip.

patterns: can a superlative be used with two things
entries.answer: A superlative marks the highest degree in a group and therefore needs at least three items, since comparing two is already a comparative. It also takes the definite article, as in the fastest car on the road, and that article is the part most often left out. A small set refuses comparison altogether, so a full glass cannot be fuller, which is why forcing a superlative can sound wrong rather than merely emphatic.

entries.answer: An attributive adjective sits directly before the noun it modifies, as in a charming house, and a predicative one follows a linking verb, as in the house is charming. The same word does both jobs with a shift in meaning, since the tired traveller describes the traveller while the traveller is tired describes a state. Some words refuse one position entirely, and the wooden chair works where the chair is wooden implies something less permanent.

entries.answer: A predicative adjective follows a linking verb and describes the subject rather than naming it, as in the soup tastes strange or the room feels cold. Linking verbs cover being, seeming and the five senses, which is where the whole class lives. The trap is that the same verbs also take ordinary objects, so he smells the milk and the milk smells sour are structurally different sentences built from the same word.

entries.answer: An abstract noun names a quality, state, action or idea that cannot be pointed at, covering honesty, freedom, arrival and kindness. The test is physical, since anything you could pick up is concrete, and that test handles the borderline cases cleanly. These are the nouns most often replaced by clumsy constructions in learner writing, because a concrete paraphrase feels safer even when it is vaguer and longer.

entries.answer: A concrete noun names something perceived directly by sight, touch, sound or smell, and it contrasts with the abstract. The distinction is not about importance, since freedom matters far more than a table, and it is not fixed either, because a word can move between classes. What actually changes with the shift is countability, since an idea takes an article while an idea of mine takes a possessive.
